chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The person in janābah must not touch a dirham or a dinar upon which is the Name of Allah, the Exalted.” And this does not contradict that.

key_terms.اسْمُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: the Divine Name of Allah, the Exalted
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janābah requiring ghusl
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a silver coin used as currency
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a gold coin used as currency
key_terms.يَمَسُّ: touches or comes into physical contact with

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janābah touch a coin bearing the Name of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity, stating that a person in janābah should not touch coins bearing the Name of Allah, the Exalted. It reflects the sanctity of the Divine Name and the jurisprudential etiquette related to taharah.
